Even though I still haven't "beaten" this game yet, I've sunk darn enough hours into it thus far to leave a review. Getting closer every time; just haven't quite crossed the finish line yet. "What? You wrote this review with 63.1 hours played? This looks like a DOS game! What's up?"

Well, be prepared for the ultimate grindfest. If you don't like grindy games, you may not like G.E.O. Because you will grind. Oh, will you grind.

So what is it? Well, in the simplest of terms, it's a mining and upgrade game. You know the drill (pun intended) - just like games like Wall World or Bore Blasters, you mine deep into the earth (or comet, or gas giant, or moon, or whatever). You get minerals. You use your mined profits to buy upgrades. That allows you to mine faster and deeper. This gives you access to more cash, which you in turn use to... upgrade, so you can mine faster and deeper. Again, if you've ever played a mining game, you know what's up.

This game comes with a ton of extra stuff you do on the side. You work on completing collections - various amounts of rocks or items. You do research. You buy stuff from the market. You play roulette, because of course you do. You build rooms for your mining base and hire employees. You fight to climb the offline leaderboard so you can become the top mining corporation. In between mining sessions, there is just a TON of stuff to collect, upgrade, and tinker with. In fact, that's one of the many things about this game that keeps drawing me back - the never ending tinkering. If you like mining, grinding, and tinkering, this game is going to be way more attractive than the videos show.

I will provide a word of caution - one of the reasons this game has SO much content is that it trickles in slowly. Again, GRINDFEST 3000. At first I got a bit discouraged, and was even considering giving up. Although it was fun, it just seemed like I was making no progress. Keep at it, though, young miner, and eventually you will be like me, drilling straight to the bottom of planets like a hot knife through butter. 

The earth you mine through is littered with goods and bads. Each block type has its own unique strength against your drill, and this is multiplied by how much gravity the planet has. You further face environmental hazards, such as burning heat or freezing cold. The further you drill, the more these effects impact you. Meanwhile, there are plenty of bonus blocks - be it increasing your cash modifier, giving you more resistance to pressure, giving you a temporary shield against environmentals, treasure chests, and much more. On the flip side, the planets are filled with monsters - and as you may have seen from other reviews, no way to kill them. Some people really don't like this, but I think it keeps you on your toes. You may be able to find the bonus item that gets rid of ALL monsters in a level, but otherwise it's a dodge-fest. Stay alert!

If you manage to drill down to the core, you can collect "cores," which you can spend in the.... whatever the heck they call that shop, to increase your stats, allow you to build more rooms on your base (which increases your stats) so you can hire more employees (which increases stats) and stuff like that. It's all about slowly but surely increasing those stats so you can drill ever deeper.

It's been so long that I can't remember if the tutorial was any good or not. I seem to not remember it being too involved. I do remember being a little confused about a couple of the things, but trial and error will teach you much.. and if you're going to play THIS game, you're going to go on mission after mission after mission.

I guess I don't fully understand why I like this game so much. Maybe it's a sunk cost fallacy at this point. I HAVE to earn the #1 spot now, and I will never give up until I do. I may push myself to gain all the collectibles and whatnot.. I cannot, at this point, give up until I've mastered this world.

It may sound like I'm not enjoying myself, but I am. I LOVE the slow and steady progress.

This is the PERFECT kind of game to listen to talking shows on YouTube or music to. (The game has its own perfectly-suited soundtrack, but a lot of times I'll just listen to some YouTuber babble about whatever). Once you get the hang of it, it doesn't take a lot of thought.. Just takes a lot, and I mean a LOT, of drilling.

Despite looking cheesy, graphics are fine. Sound effects and soundtrack suit the gameplay just fine. Controls are pretty darn easy... Bunch of clicking and moving your mouse, pretty much. (Plays on Steam Deck just fine - 63+ hours and not a single crash.) Basically, everything about it is... just fine.

I can honestly say I'm kind of a fan of the WindyBeard team. I've been grinding on this game FOREVER and NEED to finish it out... and I just bought another game of theirs, some kind of brick-breaker game, and was horrified by the fact that I may wind up in the same spot with that game that I've wound up with in G.E.O.

Basically, end of the day, this is a great game. It's not the kind of game that you beat in one sitting.. Personally, I play for a while, go play something else, come back and play a little, go play something else... and the time just racks up. You don't need to think too much - plenty of relaxing time. And again... the tinkering between digs is a collector's/tinkerer's dream.

Worth full price? Easy yes. For nine bucks I have drawn 63 hours (SO FAR... who knows how much more) out of it, so it's an EASY, EASY sell. If you can get it on sale even better - so good it should be illegal. I can't remember if I bought this full price, on sale, in a bundle or what, but even if I paid the $9, I'm very happy I did.

So if you like mining games, collecting stuff, grinding, tinkering, and relaxing... This is a game that should probably be in your library.

Geo is a space mining game where you represent a mining corporation that drills into planets, asteroids, and pretty much anything else that can be drilled into. The mechanics of this game are that you keep the resources that you drill into, each world having slightly different materials, the more types you gather, the more rooms you unlock, which can increase your resistance to the negative effects of certain planets, such as extreme heal or cold or give access to more pilots which give a variety of different bonuses.

This game is huge, there's dozens of diverse planets, bigger they are, usually the better and more rewarding things they give. Drilling also grants gold, which can be used in the Explore section to unlock more areas, used in the shop to outright buy rooms or pilots, and also used with world cores (Gotten by finishing a world) to unlock the upgrade system. Each pilot  can also be upgraded three levels, each level grants additional bonuses, from resistance against planets, or increased health, power, and speed to your drill.

Further into the game, monsters also begin to unlock, most of these can be killed with one of the many power up crates the worlds have, that of course being dynamite. While there are many perks and positive things about this game, the main issue that I've had is that on the bigger worlds, my computer slowed down to such a degree it became extremely difficult to complete that world without dying from either monsters or my health going down from the planet's high damage output. Hopefully that issue is just me, but I'd recommend playing this game with a high functioning computer.

I highly recommend this game. Well worth the full price (although I think it goes on sale for 75% off if that matters to you). I have paid far more for far less. This is currently my #1 game to play in a library full of indie games, big titles, and old classics. The interface style reminds me of MOO:2 which is also a favorite of mine in the space genre. I really enjoy mining and space in games; so GEO really scratches that itch for me.

I was initially on the fence about this game. I remember thinking it looked repetitive and lacking in challenge. I was pleasantly surprised upon actually diving into the game itself. There is a lot of strategy and planning to be had for those that are interested. Usually, this sort of game snowballs out of control in your favor when you get too wealthy. So far the game has increased in challenge for every increase in my own drill team's strength. As your power increases you unlock tougher and more varied planetary bodies with higher exploration costs. Planning your optimum route to planet cores requires quick thinking, fast reflexes, and sharp math. Getting to the bottom of a tough planet core is a thrilling triumph. Space monsters also keep you on your toes: some reflexes required.

Every drill site is made up of unique sets of tiles. Due to how the many subsystems of the game work, some tiles will be more profitable to mine, some easier to mine, some required for research, and some harmful to mine. As your drill speed increases you will need faster reflexes to choose the optimal path to reach your current goals. Having mined a core, your goals may switch mid mission from expediency (due to limited drill health) to wealth (aiming for the more valuable blocks). I won't get into all the details, but needless to say there is a lot to chew on here for those interested.

Other bonuses are the discovery of new planetary objects and crew members on your journey through space. I love the hand drawn artwork throughout. It is always a pleasure to discover a fantastic new world or a crazy new character. Often the descriptions of planets and characters are quite humorous.

Spoiler Alert: The highlight of my game so far has been discovering the planet Earth in the Phinexies 872 system. It seems humanity has abandoned it due to the rise of the Dolphin Queen.

There is a lot of grinding in this game, but I enjoy the grind. There is also no fail state which I have so far discovered, but that is also a plus in my books. You could play this game badly, and still be successful. For myself, the fun is in trying to play as efficiently as possible. 

Graphics: 9/10. Reminds me of MOO:2. Sometimes text is a little clipped out of the screen, but still readable. The hand drawn artwork is a big plus for me. The 2D graphics suit this game.

Sound: 5/10. Has it's own soundtrack, but I prefer to make my own custom music playlist for this game which includes Queen's "Under Pressure". The game itself gives solid indication of block breaking, chest smashing, and loot jingling. Lots and lots of loot jingling.

Gameplay: 10/10. Relaxing, challenging, and fun. Great after a long day of work especially if you love mining, space, and art.

Difficulty: 5/10. You can win this game no matter what you do. Just remember: "It's not whether you win or lose, it's how you play the game". Personally, being able to play without the threat of permadeath is a bonus for me.

In closing, I'd just like to add that this game is clearly a labor of love. There is fine attention to detail everywhere. For a one man indie project this game is amazing. I've also had a ton of fun with it, and look forward to more hours of enjoyment in the future. I am sure GEO 2 will be a blast.

Space mining!

Yes... buckets and buckets of Space mining!

The love.  The wanderlust.  The flying.  In spaaaaaaaace!  The drama!  Oh.. yes!

Romance?  Only with the ground that gives way after every thrust of your drill!  Oh try to not be too rough!  You just might break your drill - this can happen if you thrust too fast.  When your drill is broken no more thrusting for you... you have to give it a break and go get a new drill!

But what you really want to know is... will your drill finally make it to the core?!  Is it soft?  No it's a very hard core!  So ovum-shaped and your little drill having gone such a long way to finally penetrate its way in and cause the core to burst into long awaited rewards!  It bursts for a while there.  Enjoy it while it bursts, with rewards flying this way and that...  Bursting and bursting... it feels really good while it keeps bursting...

These are rewards you'll need to upgrade your headquarters.

In this space drama of asteroid mining you will collect various soils, minerals, and other stuff found laying around in asteroids you are trying to reach the core of to get bonuses.  You can upgrade your drill and research new rooms your employees can hang out in.

The grind comes in drilling the same asteroid repeatedly to reach the core, and there's some tension as harder rocks will break your drill faster, so you have to abandon the mission, but you can take home everything you got before the drill broke, and after leaving you can go right back in and drill some more.

For as simplistic as the game is, it's surprisingly addictive.  It's basically "click where you want to go" and some clicker elements (cores make money over time, rather than trading them in for upgrades).

This game is a little repetitive but is addictive and fun. 8/10
I will definitely try the next release.

The mechanics mixes an elemental tactical real time action with a soft management of building places and upgrading skills: the player must operate a driller spaceship for mining asteroids, moons and planets, meanwhile expands his base and hiring workers to enhance his operational efficience. There are 20 models of drillers than only can be acquiring by completing objectives, like collecting things, but are really useless except 3 or 4. There are about 60 places to mine, but reapear even traveling to supossely diferent zones. 

To complete 100% achievements takes 120 hours of dubious fun. This game has many potential even for a franchise if developer invest a lot of work in solve its desing lacks, because main concept is really good.

If you like Windybeard's new pirate game, then you will like this.  If you like the decade-old independent flash game "Glean" then you will like this.  If you enjoy mindless grinding with no real end in sight, you will enjoy this.  I enjoy all three, so I had fun with this.  Took me about 60 or 70 hours to reach Division 1.    

Here are some tips:  
1) There are no monsters in the first quadrant and the game isn't timed, so spend as much time as you like drilling the first few planets.   If you drill, for example, 100 blocks of something and you need 100 blocks for your collection, then you will earn money just for that, even if you don't get to the core or complete your research.   So you can drill the same planet like 100 times until you've got all the collections you can get from it.  [ I enjoy doing stuff like that.  If you think that sounds like a grind, this simply isn't the game for you and we'll leave it at that! :)   ]

2) You start off with a couple of crappy rooms, and only space for the two of them.  It's not obvious, but you can remove these rooms once you get better rooms.   Just pull out any people in the old room first.

3) There are slots for 6 stores but there aren't 6 stores.  Similarly there are only 89 planets even if there's slots for many more.  I have no idea why this is.   Windybeard doesn't know why this is.  No one knows why this is.  90 would have made much more sense.  

4) This is a good tip:  I tested this on a few playthroughs to compaare, so I know it's true:  crews level up in the same way every single time.  So if you hire me and I first give you a +5 Acid Resistance upgrade, I will always do so.  Always.  

5) The planets are not very random.   If you see a chest for health, then diagonally below that is a treasure chest, always just below that will be another health chest.  If you see a chest that empties the 15 squares below it, don't use it.  Dig down first, get the chest that wipes out a line across or the one that explodes an area, then use the first chest.  

6) You will die more times to Mimic treasure chests than you ever will to monsters.   After about 1 planet (maybe half that), you will know how to avoid all monsters easily with a simple serpentine rhythm to your drilling.  

7) Compared to most Steam developers ( definition of average friendly Steam Developer: C.M.Blakemore), Windybeard is helpful and friendly, still posts answers to questions in the discussion forum, and patched the game to make it easier to drill without killing your hands.  

8) Remember to blink when drilling long sites.  I myself have a tendency to stare at the screen when scanning for enemies and for chests, so this is good advice if you're like me.  

9) You will spend 99.99 of this game drilling, and 00.001% percent in your office or the stores, roulette wheel and core-atorium.  So decide in your first 2 hours if the drilling part of the game holds your interest.

10) Don't despair if you find some guy who wants 3 feathers and you only have 2 oil cans.  He will keep appearing in new quadrants until you have what he needs.

They can have monsters, or other factors that make that planet harder to drill on. (The first planet doesn't give you any sort of time constraints, but once you progress to others, time becomes a factor, so you have to make quick decisions to min-max your drill run.)

There's a lot of repetition, but only in the sense of "you're bettering yourself with each attempt." There's always something to unlock and strive for. (That actually feels worth getting!)
